introHtml:
Memramcook is one of the oldest Acadian communities in the country, and the valley between Moncton and Sackville is still full of farmhouses that have heated with oil for generations. If your tank is pushing 15 years, or your insurance company just sent a letter asking how old it is, you're not alone. Hub City Tank Co replaces and removes residential oil tanks across the whole valley, from Saint-Joseph and Pré-d'en-Haut to College Bridge and Beaumont.

We're based in Moncton, about a 25 minute run down Route 2, so getting a truck to your door is easy. Every job starts with a free written estimate, and our crews are licensed and insured for both tank replacement and tank removal. If a tank is leaking right now, skip the reading and call our 24/7 emergency line at (506) 802-3471.

sections.heading: Why So Many Memramcook Homes Still Heat with Oil
sections.html:
The Memramcook Valley never got natural gas lines, so oil has stayed the workhorse for home heating here. A lot of the houses along Route 106 and the river are older farmhouses that have been in the same family for generations, and many still run the same style of steel tank that went in decades ago. Steel tanks rust from the inside out, so a tank can look fine and still be near the end of its life.

The trouble is that insurance companies now pay close attention to tank age. Once a steel tank passes the 15 to 20 year mark, many insurers ask for proof of age or a full replacement before they'll renew your policy. That letter catches a lot of valley homeowners off guard, but it's a deadline, not a disaster, and it's fixable.

A straight swap is usually simpler and cheaper than people fear. Our oil tank replacement cost guide breaks down real numbers in Canadian dollars, and every Memramcook job starts with a free written estimate so there are no surprises.

sections.heading: Old Farmhouses, Old Tanks, and Buried Surprises
sections.html:
Older rural properties come with quirks. Basement tanks that went in long before the house was renovated, outdoor tanks sitting on tired stands, and sometimes an underground tank nobody mentioned when the property changed hands. We see all three regularly in Memramcook, especially on homesteads that date back to the days of the old Collège Saint-Joseph.

If you've spotted an unexplained fill pipe or vent line near the foundation, or a patch of ground where nothing grows, don't ignore it. An abandoned buried oil tank can leak quietly for years, and cleanup costs climb fast once oil reaches the soil or a well. We locate the tank, remove it properly, and hand you the paperwork your insurer and any future buyer will want to see.

For standard above-ground tanks, our removal service covers pumping out the leftover oil, disconnecting the lines, and hauling the tank away for proper disposal.

sections.heading: One Crew for the Whole Valley
sections.html:
We cover the entire village of Memramcook, including Saint-Joseph, Pré-d'en-Haut, College Bridge, Beaumont, La Hêtrière, and Memramcook East, along with the rural roads in between. Whether you're down near the river dykelands or up on the ridge, we can get a truck to you without any fuss.

Neighbours outside the valley are covered too. We run the same services in Sackville and Dieppe, so if you've got family nearby dealing with the same insurance letter, we can often book jobs back to back and save everyone a trip.

And if you ever smell oil or spot a wet stain under your tank, treat it as urgent. Our emergency oil tank service answers 24/7 at (506) 802-3471.

faq.q: Do you charge extra to come out to Memramcook?
faq.a: No. Memramcook sits right between Moncton and Sackville, just off Route 2, so it's inside our regular service area. Your free written estimate covers the full job, travel included, with no surprise fees.

faq.q: My insurance company wants my Memramcook oil tank replaced. How fast can you do it?
faq.a: In most cases we can replace a tank within a few days of your call, and the swap itself is usually done in a day. You get a new CSA-approved tank plus the documentation your insurer needs to renew your policy. If your renewal deadline is tight, tell us and we'll do our best to move things up.

faq.q: We bought an older farmhouse in the valley. How do we know if there's a buried oil tank?
faq.a: Look for a fill pipe or vent line near the foundation that doesn't connect to your current tank, or old copper oil lines coming through the basement wall. Those are classic signs of an abandoned underground tank. We can locate it, confirm what's down there, and remove it with proper documentation for your insurer and lawyer.

faq.q: Can you reach Memramcook in winter if my tank starts leaking?
faq.a: Yes. Route 2 and Route 106 keep the valley reachable year-round, and our emergency line runs 24/7. Call (506) 802-3471 the moment you smell oil or see a drip, because a small leak in January turns into a big cleanup fast.
